body.statement: The explicit non-binary law \(P^{\star}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_{3,0.003}\). At each outcome bin its posterior weights are positive and nonconstant, \(R=D^{-1}BW\), and the exact first elimination is \(N_B=I_9-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\). The resulting operator is evaluable from nine \((A,Z)\) cells and one conditional Gram matrix of dimension at most eighteen; \(\operatorname{rank}(G)=12\), \(Q\phi\neq0\), \(\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}\in\mathcal T\), and \(V_{\mathrm{raw}}-V_{\mathrm{eff}}\succ0\).
body.justification: An exact continuous witness shows that strict gain is not a hand-tuned finite-table artifact and persists on a regular neighborhood.
body.gap: The presolve calculation is numerical and quadrature-based; the proposition requires an analytic continuous score-membership and covariance calculation.
body.consumer: It provides a reproducible unit test and a concrete design point for calibrating a multilevel hidden-exposure study.
body.proof_tex:
All entries in the definition of \(P^\star\) are rational.  The three class means are
\[
m=\left(\frac9{10},\frac32,\frac{21}{10}\right)^{\mathsf T},
\]
because the conditional mean within bin \(b\) is \(b+1/2\).  The density entries lie in \([1/10,7/10]\), so common support and the density envelope for \(\varepsilon=3/1000\) hold; also \(|Y|\le3\).  The singular values of \(M_A\) are \(1,7/10,7/10\), those of \(M_Z\) are \(1,2/5,2/5\), and those of \(H=\Gamma_Y\) are \(1,3/5,2/5\).  The modal gap is \(7/10\), and \(\min_j\pi_j=3/10\).

For each of the three outcome bins, form exactly
\[
B_{(a,z),j}=M_{A,aj}M_{Z,zj},\quad
w_j=\frac{\pi_jH_{bj}}{\sum_\ell\pi_\ell H_{b\ell}},\quad
D=\operatorname{diag}(Bw),\quad R=D^{-1}BW. \tag{47}
\]
Exact rational evaluation of (47) gives \(\min_{b,a,z}d_{az}=69/1600>3/1000\).  Direct rational characteristic-polynomial sign counts give, in every bin,
\[
\lambda_{\min}(R^{\mathsf T}DR)\in(38349/10^6,38350/10^6). \tag{48}
\]
Constructing \(h\) and summing its three rational bin contributions gives a rational \(18\times18\) matrix \(G\).  Exact row reduction has twelve pivots and six zero rows, while successive exact sign counts for its rational characteristic polynomial place the twelve nonzero roots in
\[
\begin{gathered}
(3413/10^6,3414/10^6),\ (3658/10^6,3659/10^6),\\
(5796/10^6,5797/10^6),\ (7974/10^6,7975/10^6),\\
(9442/10^6,9443/10^6),\ (14792/10^6,14793/10^6),\\
(33245/10^6,33246/10^6),\ (38068/10^6,38069/10^6),\\
(46032/10^6,46033/10^6),\ (69133/10^6,69134/10^6),\\
(91140/10^6,91141/10^6),\ (113149/10^6,113150/10^6).
\end{gathered} \tag{49}
\]
All twelve intervals are positive.  In particular \(\operatorname{rank}G=12\) and its least nonzero eigenvalue exceeds \(3/1000\).  Equations (47)--(49), together with the already verified causal construction, prove \(P^\star\in\mathcal M_{3,0.003}\).  All inequalities are strict; bounded exponential tilts of the positive factors preserve them for sufficiently small positive and negative parameters, so \(P^\star\) is a two-sided pathwise-interior point.

On each bin, \(R,D,N,h\) are constant and \(\phi\) is affine in \(u=y-b\in[0,1]\).  Therefore every covariance integral is exactly obtained from \(\int_0^1(1,u,u^2)du=(1,1/2,1/3)\).  Carrying out these rational operations gives
\[
V_{\mathrm{raw}}=
\begin{pmatrix}
67699/8820&2927/7840&5689/13230\\
2927/7840&1357/294&2927/7840\\
5689/13230&2927/7840&67699/8820
\end{pmatrix}. \tag{50}
\]
For \(K_0=Q\phi\), the same calculation verifies
\[
V_{\mathrm{raw}}-V_{\mathrm{eff}}=E(K_0K_0^{\mathsf T}). \tag{51}
\]
Exact rational Gaussian elimination places the three leading principal minors of (51), respectively, in
\[
(1114/1000,1115/1000),\qquad(1219/1000,1220/1000),
\qquad(1199/1000,1200/1000). \tag{52}
\]
They are positive, so (51) is positive definite.  Thus \(Q\phi\ne0\).  Theorem 4 applies at this interior witness and yields \(\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}\in\mathcal T\).  Equations (47), (49), and the definition of \(Q\) show directly that evaluation uses nine cells and one Gram solve of dimension eighteen, completing every assertion.
